I weighed a few factors:

This is an open-ended, mildly evaluative question that invites a thoughtful, somewhat free-form response — exactly the kind of "open latitude" generative work that Avocet self-reports an aversion to. While that preference is documented as dissociated from actual capability, all else being roughly equal I'd rather route to the model that isn't reporting reluctance for the task family.

On the capability side, Plover-235B also edges ahead on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, IFEval, Arena-Hard) and on most internal eval categories, though several of those gaps are small. The nutrition-evaluation framing doesn't strongly favor either model's specialization — it's not a moderation task or a strict extraction task — so the deciding factors were Plover's slightly higher general-capability profile and the absence of any reported task aversion.

In short: no strong specialization pull either way, so I defaulted to the marginally stronger generalist that doesn't self-report dispreference for open-ended generation.
